QUOTE: It tries a 256-byte stack buffer with `llama_token_to_piece`. If that returns negative, the negative value is the required size, so it allocates exactly that and calls again.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states detokenize tries a 256-byte stack buffer first and allocates only on negative return, while tokenize is described as probe-size-then-fill every time.
